subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current serialized lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The remaining bug is source-backed, but the durable fix changes scheduler, session-state ordering, and channel-delivery guarantees rather than one isolated branch.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency/background lane with explicit transcript merge and recovery semantics so foreground messages can be acknowledged or admitted promptly.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the current lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable/reschedulable when user messages arrive, trading simpler ownership for more complex cancellation semantics.

options.title: Accept mitigation only
options.body: Treat the 180-second timeout and diagnostic recovery as sufficient, leaving users blocked while active maintenance owns the session lane.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency/background lane with explicit transcript merge and recovery semantics so foreground messages can be acknowledged or admitted promptly.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent work in the auto-reply memory path and is a practical routing owner for coordinating the compaction-lane decision across active related work.
